threshold_basis: Engineering and practical-significance limits declared before any Q2-Q7 challenger or holdout result. Point, probability, count, payout, runtime, and memory margins are fixed units rather than values optimized on REFEREE or holdout data.
threshold_semantics: For MINIMIZE metrics, promotion_delta is the minimum champion-minus-challenger improvement and positive degradation uses challenger-minus-champion. For MAXIMIZE metrics the signs reverse. Noninferiority, demotion, and rollback values are absolute adverse margins in the metric unit. Confidence-bound rules in promotion_policy apply before these magnitudes are compared.

metrics.definition: Mean absolute error between pre-lock median fantasy-points prediction and settled DraftKings fantasy points, macro-averaged by slate.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% slate-cluster bootstrap interval with 10000 deterministic resamples
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS over slate weights; also report players and independent slates
metrics.rationale: A tenth of a fantasy point is a small but operationally meaningful aggregate improvement; two tenths is the largest tolerated noninferiority loss.

metrics.definition: Continuous ranked probability score of each frozen player fantasy-points distribution, macro-averaged by slate.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% slate-cluster bootstrap interval with 10000 deterministic resamples
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS over slate weights; also report players and independent slates
metrics.rationale: The threshold requires distributional improvement larger than reporting noise while allowing at most a small practical regression.

metrics.definition: Absolute difference between empirical coverage and 0.80 for frozen central 80% player outcome intervals, macro-averaged by slate.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: Wilson interval clustered and summarized by slate; report nominal target
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS and independent slate count
metrics.rationale: Two percentage points is meaningful calibration improvement; five points is the maximum tolerated noninferiority gap.

metrics.definition: Brier score for pre-lock probability that a rostered player records at least one offensive snap or qualifying DST participation event.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% slate-cluster bootstrap interval with 10000 deterministic resamples
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS plus positive and negative event counts
metrics.rationale: A one-point Brier improvement is material for a gate that directly controls zero-outcome risk.

metrics.definition: Recall for settled nonparticipation among players assigned pre-lock probability below 0.50; report false-positive rate beside it.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% Wilson interval with slate-cluster sensitivity analysis
metrics.effective_sample_size: Count of independent nonparticipation events and Kish ESS
metrics.rationale: Rare inactive events need a larger five-point practical improvement and tolerate no more than a three-point regression.

metrics.definition: Salary- and field-weighted absolute error between frozen player ownership probability and settled contest ownership, macro-averaged by contest then slate.
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS plus independent contest and slate counts
metrics.rationale: One percentage point is a material ownership improvement; two points is the maximum tolerated noninferiority loss.

metrics.definition: Adaptive-bin expected calibration error for frozen ownership probabilities with bins formed on training data only.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% slate-cluster bootstrap interval with bin definitions held fixed
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS plus observations per fixed bin and independent slates
metrics.rationale: Calibration must improve by one point and cannot hide a regression larger than two points behind ranking accuracy.

metrics.definition: Mean absolute error of log1p predicted complete-lineup duplication count versus exact settled duplication, macro-averaged by contest.
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS plus unique lineups, contests, and slates
metrics.rationale: A 0.05 log-count improvement is practically visible in payout sharing; a 0.10 loss is the noninferiority ceiling.

metrics.definition: Brier score for the event that a complete lineup has no other duplicate in the settled field.
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS plus unique/nonunique event counts
metrics.rationale: A one-point Brier change is material for payout splitting and is used symmetrically for noninferiority.

metrics.definition: CRPS for the frozen contest rank-percentile distribution against exact strict-above settled rank with ties retained.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% slate-cluster bootstrap interval stratified by contest objective
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS plus entries, contests, and independent slates
metrics.rationale: A one-point rank-percentile improvement is material while a two-point loss is the noninferiority boundary.

metrics.definition: Brier score for finishing in the top 1% using exact tied ranks and the registered contest field size.
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS plus top-tail event count and independent slates
metrics.rationale: Rare-tail probabilities require at least a 0.002 Brier gain and allow no more than a 0.003 regression.

metrics.definition: Absolute error of the frozen 95th-percentile gross-payout prediction against settled gross payout, normalized by entry fee and stratified by objective.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% slate-cluster bootstrap interval with contest-objective strata
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS plus paid entries, contests, and independent slates
metrics.rationale: A tenth of an entry fee is operationally material; a quarter-entry loss is the noninferiority ceiling.

metrics.definition: Absolute error between frozen scenario expected portfolio utility and settled utility under the registered objective, normalized by total entry fees.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% slate-cluster bootstrap interval; simulation Monte Carlo interval reported separately
metrics.effective_sample_size: Kish ESS over slates plus portfolio, entry, and scenario ESS
metrics.rationale: Five percent of fees is a meaningful utility improvement; ten percent is the largest tolerated noninferiority loss.

metrics.definition: Absolute error between frozen lower-tail 5% portfolio net-payout CVaR and settled rolling-window CVaR, normalized by total entry fees.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: 95% slate-block bootstrap interval with small-tail event count reported
metrics.effective_sample_size: Tail ESS, total slate ESS, and independent portfolio count
metrics.rationale: Downside estimates must improve by ten percent of fees and regressions beyond fifteen percent are not noninferior.

metrics.definition: Wall-clock seconds for the full registered evaluation on the pinned runtime and declared hardware class.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: Median and maximum over three cold runs; no asymptotic extrapolation
metrics.effective_sample_size: Three independent cold process runs per registered scale
metrics.rationale: Runtime need not improve for model promotion but may not regress by more than 30 seconds or cross the hard deadline.

metrics.definition: Peak resident bytes during the full registered evaluation on the pinned runtime and declared hardware class.
metrics.uncertainty_interval: Maximum over three cold runs with sampler and platform reported
metrics.effective_sample_size: Three independent cold process runs per registered scale
metrics.rationale: Memory need not improve for promotion but a 256 MiB regression is the noninferiority limit and 4 GiB is a hard cap.

promotion_policy.uncertainty_rule: The appropriate one-sided 95% slate-cluster interval must clear the registered promotion delta for primary metrics and remain inside every noninferiority margin; point estimates alone never promote.
promotion_policy.multiple_testing_control: Holm correction at family-wise alpha 0.05 within each metric domain; every domain must pass.
promotion_policy.rollback_on_threshold_breach: One rollback_delta breach or two consecutive demotion_delta windows
promotion_policy.referee_policy: REFEREE is report-only for tuning and selection but its registered safety or sign disagreement blocks promotion.
